chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Jelly Roll Morton on the corner and his talking mouth
summary: Jelly Roll held court in front of the Rhythm Club, and Danny notes the twitching muscles at the corner of his mouth, like Bill Robinson's.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Jelly Roll stood on the corner. They didn't understand Jelly Roll. Jelly Roll would be talkin' like he talked to night people, who understand Jelly Roll... Jelly Roll would stand out in front of the club and talk to all these defeated musicians; half of them couldn't play, including me. We'd stand around there waiting for a gig and looking up at Jelly Roll. Well, Jelly Roll is from home. But Jelly Roll, he loves an audience. I noticed Jelly Roll had two little things on the end of his jaw that he could establish in ...(?)... When he wasn't talkin', these little muscles would be moving. Bill Robinson had the same thing. Yeah-yeah-yeah... See, look.
Mmm-hmm. They're almost repeating the words you said because they want to get a word in.
No, just of those, at the corner of their mouth.

Then he'd prop his mouth, and you'd wait for an answer, then he'd lower his lips to get the right retort, if he was right. If he was wrong, he'd push his mouth again. That's a whole act with this mouth, see. My old folks said a mouth can get you in a whole lot of trouble. You see? And he'd have his mouth propped up, Jelly Roll.

And he's waiting. And his lips is juicy, not dry at all. Bill Robinson had the same kind of mouth. He would do the same thing. He was waiting. He wanted to be the leader and wanted to support the talk -- get the last word in there. If he didn't get the last one, he was liable to start to pull his pistols out. [LAUGHS]
